previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for episodic left-sided chest pain that had increased in frequency, raising concern for unstable angina given his history of coronary artery disease and prior CABG. Initial evaluation showed a mildly elevated troponin and unremarkable EKG and chest X-ray. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed severe native three-vessel coronary disease and diseased bypass grafts, but no lesions amenable to intervention. Management was optimized medically with increased isosorbide mononitrate, initiation of clopidogrel, and transition to metoprolol XL. During admission, he reported suprapubic discomfort from his chronic indwelling Foley catheter; it was changed due to mixed flora on urinalysis, though no antibiotic treatment was initiated as he remained afebrile. He also received neurology consultation for bilateral hand numbness and neck pain, diagnosed as carpal tunnel syndrome and cervical radiculopathy, with recommendations for wrist splints and a soft neck collar. Constipation was treated with lactulose. He was discharged home with improved symptoms, clear instructions on medication changes, and follow-up plans.

Coronary atherosclerosis of autologous vein bypass graft

metoprolol) that morning in the hospital but only took his 
night-time medications as directed. He was sitting in a lounge 
chair for about 30 minutes talking to a friend on the phone, 
then got up and walked through the parlor to the bathroom with 
his walker. He reached the bathroom and put his walker aside 
(usually does this to go to the bathroom). Denied any heralding 
symptoms during this time such as chest pain, shortness of 
breath, LH, dizziness, palpitations, nausea, or vomiting. Did 
feel a bit sweaty at the time. No major pain exacerbations, 
although did notice the dull pain in his R groin. Suddenly, he 
states he unexpectedly passed out. He hit left side of head on 
floor and per daughter heard the noise and came into the 
bathroom and found him on the ground after he fell, so the fall 
was partially witnessed. Per report, he had 30 seconds of 
unresponsiveness, followed by moaning for 15 seconds. No seizure 
activity. His eyes appeared to have rolled into the back of his 
head. No nausea, vomiting, tongue biting, loss of bowel/bladder 
or other seizure activity, but after awakening was complaining 
of head pain from the fall. He was not post-ictal and remembers 
the ride to the ambulance.

Hct of 42.8 (stable). CT Head showed a small SAH. Neurosurgery 
consulted, no surgical intervention, recommended repeat Head CT 
in AM. Subconjunctival hemorrhage in the L eye was noted but he 
had a flourescine exam which showed no abrasion  
.  
On the floor, the patient admits to some mild dullness in his R 
groin, but denies any headache or head pain, chest pain, 
shortness of breath. He still also has discomfort in his 
suprapubic region from his catheter. Also has some tingling in 
his left hand which is chronic and thought to be due to carpal 
tunnel.

vasovagal/hypotension given recent increase in imdur and change

He was monitored on telemetry and two sets of cardiac enzumes 
were negative.  His imdur was initially held and was re-started

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Fall.

COMPARISON:  CT available from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images of the cervical spine were obtained
without the use of IV contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were
performed at 2-mm slice thickness.

FINDINGS:  No acute fracture or traumatic malalignment of the cervical spine
is seen.  In comparison to the ___ study, no changes seen in
multilevel degenerative changes, most pronounced from C4 through C6, including
posterior osteophytosis and significant intervertebral disc space narrowing
and subchondral sclerosing.  Mild neural foraminal and moderate thecal sac
narrowing is redemonstrated at this level.  Grade 1 anterolisthesis of C7 on
T1 is stable.  Bulging and calcification of the soft tissues posterior to the
atlantoaxial joints is again seen.  There is an old fracture of a nuchal
ligament (701B:19).  The patient is status post median sternotomy.  No
prevertebral soft tissue abnormalities are seen.  Included views of the lung
apices are normal. A small right sphenoid retention cyst is seen. 

IMPRESSION:  Severe multilevel degenerative changes throughout the cervical
spine, resulting in moderate narrowing of the thecal sac, worst at C4 through
C6.  Overall, these findings are unchanged since the ___,
examination.  No superimposed fracture is seen.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images of the head were obtained without the
use of IV contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed at 2-mm
slice thickness.

FINDINGS:  
A tiny subarachnoid hemorrhage is seen within the right frontal lobe (2:22). 
This was not present on the ___ examination.  No mass effect is
seen.  No other bleed, mass, mass effect, or large vascular territorial
infarction is seen.  A small soft tissue contusion overlies the left frontal
aspect of the calvarium (2:16), with no subjacent fracture seen.  The middle
ear cavities and mastoid air cellsare clear.  There is a small right sphenoid
mucous retention cyst. The orbits are symmetric in size and intact.

A 9-mm calcified mass within the left posterior fossa (2:9) is unchanged,
likely reflecting a meningioma.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Tiny right frontal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
2.  Left frontal superficial contusion, with no subjacent fracture.
3.  Unchanged 9-mm left posterior fossa meningioma.

FINDINGS:  AP upright and lateral views of the chest are obtained.  Midline
sternotomy wires and post-CABG changes are again noted.  There is stable
elevation of the left hemidiaphragm with left basilar atelectasis.  Mild right
basilar atelectasis is also noted.  On a prior CT, the patient is noted to

of nodular opacity seen on chest radiograph in the left upper lobe.  Heart
size cannot be readily assessed.  Mediastinal contour appears stable.  No sign
of pleural effusion.  Bony structures are notable for degenerative changes in
the thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intrathoracic process.  Stable chronic changes.

INDICATION:  Status post fall and small frontal subarachnoid hemorrhage,
evaluate for interval change.

TECHNIQUE:  Sequential axial images were acquired through the head without
administration of intravenous contrast.

COMPARISON:  CT head from ___.

FINDINGS:  This study is partially limited due to patient motion. Within these
limitations, the follwoing are the findings. The previously identified small
hyperdense focus in the sulcus/adjacent cortex in the right frontal lobe at
the vertex  is not identified on today's study.  There is no evidence of acute
intracranial hemorrhage, edema, shift of normally midline structures,
hydrocephalus, or acute large vascular territorial infarction.  Prominence of
the ventricles and sulci are consistent with age-related involutional changes.
A mucoid retention cyst or polyp is seen in the right sphenoid sinus.  The
remainder of the visualized portions of the paranasal sinuses and mastoid air
cells are well aerated.  There is no acute fracture identified.  A 9-mm
ossified lesion in the left posterior fossa is again noted, most consistent
with a meningioma.  The left frontal subgaleal hematoma is decreased in size. 
Vascular calcifications are noted.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of intracranial hemorrhage on today's study.  The previously
identified hyperdense focus over the right frontal lobe is no longer
visualized.

2.  Mucoid retention cyst or polyp in the right sphenoid sinus.

3.  Left posterior fossa ossified lesion,likely  meningioma, minimally
increased since ___ CT. Followup as clinically  indicated.
